title: General Chemistry I & II
description: General Chemistry I & II develops molecular explanations and quantitative models for matter, energy, reactions, equilibrium, measurement, and chemical systems. Across two semesters, students connect macroscopic observations to particulate and symbolic representations. They solve multistep problems with units and assumptions, conduct safe, reproducible laboratory work, evaluate uncertainty, and apply chemistry to process systems, environmental media, foods, nutrients, and human physiology.

topics.title: Chemical Foundations, Measurement, Safety, and Scientific Practice
topics.description: Chemistry starts with defensible measurement. This unit establishes the language, laboratory habits, uncertainty awareness, and safety judgment required across both semesters.

children.title: Matter, models, and chemical reasoning
children.description: Students learn to move among observable behavior, particle-level explanations, and symbolic representations.

children.title: Physical versus chemical properties and changes
Units, dimensional analysis, and quantitative communication
children.description: Units become a calculation method and a built-in test of whether a result is plausible.

children.title: SI units, prefixes, and derived quantities
Conversion factors, density, and multistep calculations
Significant figures, scientific notation, and order-of-magnitude checks
Uncertainty, safety, and research integrity
children.description: Reliable chemistry protects people while preserving a traceable chain from observation to conclusion.

children.title: Accuracy, precision, random error, and systematic error
ACS RAMP, SDS/GHS information, PPE, waste, and emergency response
Laboratory notebooks, data provenance, reproducibility, and ethical reporting

topics.title: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and the Quantum Model
topics.description: Atomic models explain periodic behavior, spectroscopy, bonding, and the origin of chemical identity. The emphasis is prediction from evidence rather than memorization.

children.title: Atomic composition and isotopes
children.description: Nuclear composition connects elemental identity to charge, mass, abundance, and analytical signatures.

children.title: Protons, neutrons, electrons, ions, and isotopic notation
Average atomic mass and isotopic abundance
Light, quantization, and atomic spectra
children.description: Discrete interactions between matter and light reveal that atomic energy is quantized.

children.title: Wavelength, frequency, energy, and the electromagnetic spectrum
Photons, line spectra, absorption, and emission
Orbitals, electron configurations, and periodic trends
children.description: A quantum model of electrons supports systematic predictions across the periodic table.

children.title: Quantum numbers, orbital shapes, and nodes
Pauli exclusion, Hund's rule, and electron configurations
Effective nuclear charge, shielding, radius, ionization energy, and electron affinity

topics.title: Chemical Bonding, Molecular Geometry, and Electronic Structure
topics.description: Bonding models turn electron arrangements into three-dimensional structures and explain polarity, stability, reactivity, and material properties.

children.title: Ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding
children.description: Students compare limiting bonding models while recognizing that real bonding lies on a continuum.

children.title: Lewis structures, resonance, and formal charge
children.description: Electron-counting models provide a disciplined first description of molecules and polyatomic ions.

children.title: Geometry, hybridization, and molecular orbitals
children.description: Three-dimensional and orbital models connect structure to measurable properties.

children.title: VSEPR domains, shapes, bond angles, and polarity
Bond order, delocalization, magnetism, and simple MO diagrams

topics.title: Chemical Quantities, Equations, and Stoichiometry
topics.description: Stoichiometry converts balanced equations into quantitative models of material use, product formation, emissions, nutrient composition, and process efficiency.

children.title: The mole and chemical composition
children.description: The mole links microscopic particles to laboratory-scale mass and composition.

children.title: Avogadro constant, molar mass, and particle counting
Chemical equations and reaction classes
children.description: Balanced equations preserve atoms and charge while organizing common patterns of reactivity.

children.title: Complete ionic and net ionic equations
Combination, decomposition, combustion, precipitation, acid-base, and redox reactions
Reaction stoichiometry and material balances
children.description: Coefficients provide mole ratios for predicting requirements, yields, and residual material.

children.title: Limiting reactant, excess reactant, and theoretical yield
Percent yield, purity, atom economy, and elemental balances

topics.title: Aqueous Reactions and Solution Preparation
topics.description: Water is the principal medium for environmental, nutritional, biological, and many industrial systems. Students learn to prepare solutions and predict what species are actually present.

children.title: Concentration and dilution
children.description: Concentration measures translate composition into quantities usable for experiments, formulations, and treatment decisions.

children.title: Molarity, molality, mole fraction, and mass/volume percent
Parts per million and parts per billion
Solution preparation, serial dilution, and mixing calculations
Electrolytes and ionic reactions
children.description: Dissolved substances behave differently depending on ion formation and reaction driving forces.

children.title: Spectator ions and net ionic equations
Solution stoichiometry and titrimetric foundations
children.description: Measured solution volumes can determine unknown composition through reaction stoichiometry.

children.title: Equivalence point, endpoint, indicators, and basic titration calculations

topics.title: Gases and Molecular Motion
topics.description: Gas models connect pressure, volume, temperature, composition, and particle motion to atmosphere, respiration, combustion, and process operations.

children.title: Empirical gas laws and the ideal gas equation
children.description: Simple proportional relationships combine into a model that predicts gas-state changes.

children.title: Boyle, Charles, Avogadro, and combined gas laws
Mixtures, reactions, and gas collection
children.description: Gas composition and reaction stoichiometry support environmental and process calculations.

children.title: Gas stoichiometry and collection over water
Mole fraction, humidity awareness, and combustion gases
Kinetic molecular theory and nonideality
children.description: Particle motion explains gas laws and clarifies when ideal assumptions fail.

children.title: Temperature, average kinetic energy, and molecular speed
Intermolecular attractions, molecular volume, and real-gas deviations

topics.title: Intermolecular Forces, Liquids, Solids, and Phase Behavior
topics.description: Intermolecular attractions and solid structure explain boiling, viscosity, solubility, phase changes, and the behavior of foods, contaminants, and process materials.

children.title: Intermolecular forces and bulk properties
children.description: Students infer physical properties from the strength and type of attractions among particles.

children.title: Dispersion, dipole-dipole, hydrogen bonding, and ion-dipole forces
Surface tension, capillarity, viscosity, and volatility
Phase changes and phase diagrams
children.description: Energy and pressure determine which phase is stable and how transitions occur.

children.title: Phase diagrams, triple point, critical point, and supercritical fluids
Solids and structure-property relationships
children.description: Classification of solids connects bonding and arrangement to mechanical, electrical, and thermal behavior.

children.title: Molecular, ionic, metallic, and network solids
Unit cells, packing, defects, and diffraction awareness

topics.title: Thermochemistry and the First Law
topics.description: Energy accounting explains heat flow, work, fuel value, metabolic energy, and the thermal consequences of reactions and phase changes.

children.title: Systems, heat, work, and internal energy
children.description: A clear system boundary and sign convention make energy balances consistent.

children.title: System, surroundings, state functions, and path functions
Heat, pressure-volume work, and the first law
Calorimetry and heat capacity
children.description: Temperature measurements can be converted into reaction or phase-change energy.

children.title: Calorimeter calibration, heat loss, and uncertainty
Enthalpy, Hess's law, and formation data
children.description: State functions let students construct difficult reaction energies from accessible pathways.

children.title: Bond-enthalpy estimates, combustion, and food-energy context

topics.title: Solutions, Solubility, and Colligative Properties
topics.description: Solution formation balances molecular interactions and dispersal. This unit supports separation, formulation, osmotic, and contaminant-partition reasoning.

children.title: Energetics and entropy of dissolution
children.description: Dissolution depends on competing solute-solute, solvent-solvent, and solute-solvent interactions.

children.title: Solubility of gases and condensed solutes
children.description: External conditions change how much material can remain dissolved.

children.title: Pressure, temperature, salinity, and matrix effects
Vapor pressure and colligative properties
children.description: Particle number, not chemical identity alone, controls several important solution properties.

children.title: Osmotic pressure, van't Hoff factor, tonicity, and membrane context

topics.title: Entropy, Gibbs Energy, and Chemical Thermodynamics

children.title: Entropy and the second law
children.description: Entropy provides a statistical measure of energy dispersal and a criterion for spontaneous change.

children.title: Entropy changes of system and surroundings
Second and third laws and standard molar entropy
Gibbs energy and spontaneity
children.description: Gibbs energy combines enthalpy and entropy for constant-temperature, constant-pressure systems.

children.title: Delta G = Delta H - T Delta S
Free energy, equilibrium, and coupled processes
children.description: Thermodynamics links reaction driving force to composition and shows how unfavorable processes can be driven.

children.title: Delta G standard and equilibrium constant
Chemical potential awareness, coupling, and energy efficiency

topics.title: Chemical Kinetics, Mechanisms, and Catalysis
topics.description: Kinetics determines how fast change occurs and which molecular pathway is followed, informing reactors, pollutant fate, nutrient degradation, enzymes, and shelf life.

children.title: Rates, rate laws, and reaction order
children.description: Experimental concentration-rate relationships reveal kinetic behavior without assuming a mechanism.

children.title: Differential rate laws, orders, and rate constants
Integrated laws and temperature dependence
children.description: Concentration-time data and temperature variation quantify lifetime and activation barriers.

children.title: Zero-, first-, and second-order integrated laws
Arrhenius equation, activation energy, and Arrhenius plots
Mechanisms and catalysis
children.description: Elementary steps must reproduce both the net reaction and observed kinetics.

topics.title: Chemical Equilibrium and Coupled Systems
topics.description: Equilibrium is a dynamic balance that predicts composition and response in reactors, natural waters, foods, and living systems.

children.title: Equilibrium constants and reaction quotient
children.description: Mass-action expressions distinguish current composition from equilibrium composition.

children.title: Kc, Kp, heterogeneous equilibria, and dimensionless-activity awareness
Reaction quotient Q and direction of change
Manipulating equations and combining equilibrium constants
Equilibrium calculations

children.title: Quadratic, numerical, and mass-balance solution awareness
Perturbation and process design

children.title: Concentration, pressure, volume, inert-gas, and temperature changes
Catalysts, yield-rate tradeoffs, and coupled-equilibrium awareness

topics.title: Acids, Bases, Buffers, and Titrations

children.title: Acid-base models and strength

children.title: Conjugate pairs, amphiprotic species, and water autoionization
Strong versus weak acids and bases, Ka, Kb, and pKa
PH of strong, weak, and polyprotic systems

children.title: Weak-acid and weak-base equilibria and percent ionization

Buffers and titration curves

children.title: Equivalence, endpoint, indicator selection, and physiological/food buffers

topics.title: Solubility Equilibria, Complexation, and Water Chemistry

children.title: Solubility product and precipitation

children.title: Complex ions and coupled equilibria

children.title: Natural and applied water chemistry

children.title: Alpha, beta, positron, electron-capture, and gamma processes

children.title: Metals, ceramics, glasses, polymers, and composites

Environmental Science applications

children.title: Carbonate chemistry, redox, sorption, partitioning, and contaminant fate
Atmospheric photochemistry, aerosols, greenhouse gases, and acid deposition awareness
Sampling, risk, remediation, green chemistry, and environmental justice
Nutrition and Dietetics applications and capstone
children.description: Molecular interactions, equilibria, and measurement underpin food composition, nutrient function, digestion, and quality.

children.title: Buffers, electrolytes, osmosis, minerals, and biochemical redox context
Food energy, solubility, emulsions, oxidation, preservation, and nutrient analysis
Integrated inquiry: question, RAMP plan, calibration, uncertainty, reproducible analysis, decision memo, and oral defense
